summary.headline: Standalone revenue rose 162% YoY to INR2,000 million in Q1 CY26 with EBITDA of INR114 million, while consolidated EBITDA margin was only 1.4%.
summary.overview: John Cockerill India reported its first quarter of consolidated results, including China, Belgium and Germany entities from January 2026. Standalone revenue grew 162% YoY to INR2,000 million and standalone EBITDA turned positive at INR114 million (about 5.7% margin), but management attributed margin pressure to hiring costs, a mix shift toward large projects, and one-off integration expenses. Consolidated revenue was INR3.4 billion (+56% YoY) with EBITDA of INR49 million (1.4% margin). Consolidated order book was about INR33 billion and standalone order book about INR13 billion (+101% YoY). Management targets a consolidated EBITDA margin of around 3% now and more than 10% over three years, while fundraising and USA consolidation timing remain undecided.

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,000 million and EBITDA INR114 million in Q1 CY26; margin dented by hiring upfront costs, a shift to large projects from value-added services, and consolidation one-offs. Management expects margin improvement from next quarter as Q1 and H2 FY25 orders convert.

segments.name: Consolidated (incl. China, Belgium, Germany)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.4 billion and EBITDA INR49 million (1.4% margin) in first consolidated quarter, hit by integration costs and consolidation adjustments. Order book about INR33 billion, mostly executable over about three years; value services portion 12-18 months.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin currently around 3%, to rise step by step; management aims for more than 10% over the next three years, with mid-path progress expected by start of next year.
Cost restructuring from West to East (India/China) planned over 18 months; benefits expected over 12-18 months.
Margin improvement expected from next quarter as recently won orders start converting.
Value services targeted at 30-35% of mix over the next three to five years.
Management expects new technology (JVD, Volteron) revenue in coming quarters; Volteron has no revenue yet and its commercial strategy is being reshaped.
Rolls coating facility at Taloja expected to be commissioned shortly; capex described as limited for an engineering company.
capex_capacity: Rolls coating facility at Taloja expected to be commissioned shortly, introducing coating capabilities in India with faster turnaround.
Capex described as limited because JCIL is an engineering company; main P&L effect is R&D and new-technology costs, not capex.
Old machines dismantled at Taloja last year to create space for the coating line, generating asset-sale income.
JVD technology still being fine-tuned; revenue expected in coming quarters. Volteron commercialisation expected on a medium-term horizon.
demand_pricing: JSW Steel CGL project order won in the quarter, valued at approximately INR4.4-4.7 billion.
Management expects positive order trend over 24 months, led by India (capacity doubling by 2030) and China, plus growing interest in JVD green-steel technology.

Europe described as a standby market; management expects new EU import quotas to drive demand next year. US seen as a market with the best steel price per ton, with consolidation and Nippon Steel's US Steel purchase expected to drive investment.
Relationship with SAIL under an MoU signed a little over a year ago; management would not disclose details, saying projects are being built up.
Consolidated order book executable mainly over about three years; value services over 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating leverage not show despite record revenue, and why did employee costs rise 34% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited three factors: upfront hiring and organisational realignment costs, a mix shift toward large projects (JSW, Tata) versus value-added services, and one-off consolidation/integration expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated order book executability?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the approximately INR33 billion is executable over about three years; a smaller value services portion runs 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Post-consolidation margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated EBITDA about 3% currently; target above 10% over three years, with mid-path progress by the start of next year, via a West-to-East cost shift over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraise deferred? Promoter stake and USA consolidation timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Board still exploring funding options with another board meeting planned in 2-3 weeks. Promoter stake to stay at current level for now. USA consolidation faces technical issues; target by end of year or a slight postponement.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition price versus revenue for the European, Chinese and US businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total SPA price is around EUR50 million including USA; the analyst's arithmetic was disputed and the discussion was taken offline.

qa_highlights.question: Composition of other income of about INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly interest income plus sale of old assets and scrap; Q1 other income stated as INR93 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone and consolidated margins converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects convergence through moving activity to India/China, converting R&D into orders, and structural streamlining over 12-18 months; iron and steel (upstream) has no contract in hand yet.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 1.4% versus standalone margin of about 5.7%; delivery of the targeted ~3% and later 10%+ depends on cost realignment.
JVD and Volteron R&D costs are running ahead of revenue; Volteron IP sits with the promoter and strategy is under discussion.
Fundraise plan deferred; board decision expected in 2-3 weeks. Promoter stake change possible.
USA business consolidation timing uncertain (end of year or postponement) with technical issues.
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and European energy costs may cause short-term volatility.
Transcript shows analyst disputes over acquisition pricing and other income, taken offline; watch for disclosure follow-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order momentum and long-term positioning, but notably cautious and at times evasive on margins, funding, USA consolidation and Volteron, with several answers deferred to later discussions. Management acknowledged current EBITDA is "not what we are looking for."
key_quotes: We are right now, let's say, fine-tuning our strategy for the next months to come and we'll be able to communicate more on Volteron.

So, we are aiming right now, we have an EBITDA at around consolidated at around 3% and it will go step by step, not by way over what we are aiming is really be at more than 10% over the next three years.
We see right now more the cost than the benefit. The benefits will come in the next quarters.
So, either we are able to achieve that by the end of the year or maybe it will be discussion on maybe postponing slightly, but not so much. It's just timing.
